st.headline: Japanese carmakers to cut development times to counter Chinese rivals
st.teaser: They typically spend around four years developing a new model, more than twice that of their Chinese rivals.
fullText: TOKYO – Japanese carmakers are stepping up efforts to shorten their vehicle development times as they seek to catch up with Chinese rivals that offer new models to global markets more quickly, to better respond to changing customer demand.

Toyota Motor, Honda Motor, Nissan Motor and other Japanese carmakers typically spend around four to five years developing a new model, more than twice as long as the less than two years taken by Chinese companies.

As part of its reform measures, Nissan aims to slash development times under its new family-based vehicle development strategy. The carmaker will design a common platform for multiple models of the same size.
The carmaker, for example, plans to shorten the lead time for developing a new sport-utility vehicle model to three years and one month for launch in North America in 2028.
It will then use the same platform as that of the new SUV for its derivative models, enabling it to reduce development time by up to 40% to 2½ years.
The new product strategy will cover 80% of the company’s global sales and is expected to cut the number of part types by 70%.
“This is a reform to become a company that responds to changes and delivers good cars in a timely manner,” Hidemi Sasaki, deputy general manager of Nissan’s product planning division, said.

Honda, seeking a V-shaped recovery from its first net loss in the last fiscal year, has introduced the “Triple Half” approach designed to halve development costs, time frames and workloads from 2025 levels, making full use of artificial intelligence and other digital technologies.
The new initiatives will begin with new models whose development the company will start in 2028.
Toyota, the world’s largest carmaker by volume, is also working to reduce types of parts, depending on customer needs, as fewer parts will improve productivity and speed up development work.
Naming the project Area 35, Toyota aims to improve the use of plant floor space by 35%.
Suzuki Motor plans to halve its current development time to around two years, while Mitsubishi Motors also aims to shorten the period by 20% to three years by around 2030. KYODO NEWS

cna.headline: PAP votes in top decision-making body, Jeffrey Siow and Jasmin Lau nominated but not voted in
cna.teaser: Sunday’s ballot was the first for secretary-general Lawrence Wong since he led the party through his first General Election as prime minister last year.
fullText: SINGAPORE: The People’s Action Party (PAP) has elected its next central executive committee (CEC), as cadres voted in a renewed leadership slate at the party’s conference on Sunday (Oct 25).
First-term Members of Parliament Jeffrey Siow and Jasmin Lau made the nomination list for the party’s top decision-making body, but were not voted in.

Sunday’s ballot was the first for secretary-general Lawrence Wong since he led the party through his first General Election as prime minister last year. The PAP conference takes place every two years.
In no particular order, the PAP’s 39th CEC comprises:
These 12 members were elected from a secret ballot of 19 candidates earlier in the morning.

Minister for Energy, Trade and Industry (Energy and Industry) Tan See Leng and Acting Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs Zaqy Mohamad were then co-opted into the CEC with the 13th and 14th highest number of votes among party cadres. The PAP’s constitution allows for up to six members to be co-opted.

Party insiders told CNA that the other five candidates on the ballot were: Marsiling-Yew Tee GRC MP Alex Yam, Acting Minister for Manpower Jasmin Lau, Minister for Transport Jeffrey Siow, Minister for Digital Development and Information Josephine Teo, Second Minister for Home Affairs and Foreign Affairs Sim Ann.
First-term minister David Neo was not on the list of nominees.
CNA understands that Mr Wong, Mr Lee Hsien Loong, Mr Desmond Lee, Mr Chan, Mr Masagos, Mr Shanmugam and Ms Fu were identified as the core leaders of this team.
Other co-opted members, as well as specific appointments within the committee – such as chairman, secretary-general, treasurer and organising secretaries – will be announced in the weeks ahead.
The timing for this has varied in the past. It took 10 days in 2024, 20 days in 2022, and 11 days in 2020.
At Sunday’s conference, Mr Wong said the party cannot expect younger Singaporeans to feel the same bond with it simply for its past work, and must connect with them on their own terms.

“The strong mandate we received at the last election does not guarantee continued support,” he said. “We must continue to earn the trust of Singaporeans through what we deliver, how we conduct ourselves, and how well we serve Singaporeans.”

He called for the party to have the courage to make difficult decisions and the determination to see them through, and to remain a party for Singaporeans across generations, communities and all walks of life.
“The world around us may be growing darker. But together, we will keep our little red dot shining brightly. Together, we will secure a brighter future for all Singaporeans,” said Mr Wong.

mom.headline: Additional Guidance for Employers on Use of 1-Hour PM2.5 Readings to Protect Outdoor Workers During Haze
mom.teaser: 1 The Ministry of Manpower (MOM) has issued new guidance on how employers should adjust outdoor work based on the 1-hour PM2.5 readings. This complements the existing guidance based on the PSI forecast, and helps employers respond within the day as air quality changes.
